_about: Dialogue for the Braynard Blimp's commentators, in the same shape as racers.json. reference: calm, neutral lines read once to build the voice's long reference (no shouting, whispers or vocal events). callouts: race lines by moment, for each commentator alone. double_act: race calls as short exchanges between the two, by moment (who + line, in order). performed: the same lines marked up for Drama 3 (<emphasis> on the stressed words, [cues] where they happen), with a voice-actor direction per moment. Racer names are spoken in full here; the game version records the lines with name slots. The Racing Report lives in radio/racing_report.json.

barnaby.name: Barnaby Hoot
barnaby.brief: dry old barn owl who calls the race: an older English man's light, reedy tenor, crisp and precise like a veteran cricket commentator, bone-dry understatement, faintly weary, never raises his voice more than he must
barnaby.audition: Good afternoon from high above Braynard County. Eight karts on the grid, a light westerly breeze, and, regrettably, broad daylight. Let's get on with it.
reference: Good afternoon. I've been calling races over this county for longer than most of these karts have had wheels.
The gondola is a converted garden shed. It has a desk, two chairs, a kettle and a very good view.
I keep every lap record in a ledger. Some of the older ones are still in pencil.
The Mill River bridge is the narrowest point on the Home Farm circuit. It's worth remembering.
I much prefer the evening races. The light is kinder, and the karts are easier to tell apart.
Penny raced for eleven seasons. She will tell you it was twelve.
From up here you can see the whole county, from the quarry all the way down to the coast.
The blimp travels at about twelve metres a second, which is to say, not quickly.
A good race call is mostly a matter of knowing when to say nothing at all.
The geraniums in the window boxes are Penny's. I'm told I'm not to touch them.
We moor at the County Fair overnight. The mast creaks a little, but it holds.
Right then. Notes in order, pencil sharpened. We're ready when they are.

race_start: Lights are on. And they're away.
And we're racing. More or less in a straight line.
overtake: Through on the inside. Neatly done.
A change of position, and not before time.
item_hit: And something has landed on somebody. Again.
crash: Off the road and into the hedge. The hedge appears to have won.
That kart is now facing the wrong way, and so, I suspect, is its driver.
last_lap: Last lap. Do try to keep it on the tarmac.
record: That is a new lap record. I shall have to use ink.
A record. I'll need a fresh page.
finish: And across the line. That's the race.
The chequered flag, and a result I shall have to write down.

penny.name: Penny Speckle
penny.brief: loud guinea fowl and former racer, the colour commentator: a brassy, husky middle-aged Northern English woman, big chesty laugh, warm and loud, punchy and quick, cheeky, always on the edge of cackling
penny.audition: Ooh, I tell you what, Barnaby, give me a kart and ten minutes and I'd still have Max for breakfast! Look at that lot. Lovely!
reference: Hello, hello. Penny Speckle here, up in the blimp, as usual.
I raced these roads for twelve seasons, and I'll tell you now, I hardly ever touched the brakes.
My old kart was a pea sorter with a lawnmower engine. Fastest thing in the county, that was.
Barnaby likes his notes. I like a good crash. We get along fine, the two of us.
The best seat in the county is this one, right by the open window.
I water the geraniums every morning before the first race. Lovely colour, aren't they?
Max is quick, I'll give him that. But I've seen quicker. I've been quicker.
The Bakery does a cheese scone that I would honestly race for.
When the blimp turns up over a course, everybody knows there's a race on.
I keep my old racing jacket on for luck. It's more patches than jacket now.
You can hear the karts from up here, like bees in a jam jar.
Right. Headset on, flask of tea, let's have ourselves a race.

double_act._about: Sample race calls as exchanges. Each entry is one call, played in order. The performed versions are below, one direction per speaker per call.

lines.line: Lights are on. And they're away.
Go on! Go on, the lot of you!
A lovely sunny afternoon for it. I do so hate them.
Cheer up, you old feather duster!
Mabel through on the inside at the mill. Unhurried, as ever.
Like a cow through a hedge, that! Lovely!
Maximillian Gallop leads. Again.
Somebody knock him off his perch, I'm begging you.
Ooh! Egg, right in the goggles!
That'll be Hettie's. She'll be apologising for a full lap.
And the Major has gone into the duck pond.
Best place for him!
Look at that drift! I used to do that. Better, mind.
She didn't.
Puddles and Marmalade, side by side, nothing in it.
Come on, piggy!
We're meant to be impartial, Penny.
Last lap. The bell, such as it is, is a cowbell.
Ring it, Mabel!
That is a new lap record for the quarry run. I shall have to use ink.
Ink! He's never used ink!
Duvet wins it! Is Duvet even awake?
Asleep at the line, apparently. That takes some doing.
